outputs.L4:
A position-measuring device determines the position of a first body relative to a second body. A scale band carrying a striped marker pattern is attached to one of the bodies, while a detection unit containing two sensors is mounted on the other. As the bodies move relative to one another, the sensors scan the marker pattern and generate signals corresponding to the transitions between adjacent stripes.

The scale band is divided longitudinally into two separate tracks, each of which is monitored by one of the sensors. The stripe transitions in the tracks are arranged at different, individually defined inclination angles relative to the longitudinal direction of the scale band. Consequently, the points at which the two sensors detect a transition depend on both the sensor locations and the particular inclination of that transition. The resulting combination of sensor signals therefore provides a distinctive code for each measured position.

By comparing the signals from the two tracks and identifying the associated transition angles, the device can determine the current relative position of the bodies directly from the marker pattern. Because the differently inclined transitions form uniquely recognizable position markers, the system avoids ambiguity between otherwise similar stripe sequences and can continue to provide reliable measurements even during extended movement. This arrangement enables robust and accurate relative-position detection using a compact scale band and only two sensing elements.
outputs.L5:
### A Measuring Device

A measuring device is an instrument used to determine the size, amount, or degree of something. Measuring devices are essential in everyday life, science, medicine, engineering, and industry because they provide accurate and reliable information.

There are many types of measuring devices. A ruler measures length, a thermometer measures temperature, a scale measures weight, and a clock measures time. More advanced devices, such as digital multimeters, can measure electrical values like voltage, current, and resistance.

Modern measuring devices often use electronic sensors and digital displays. They are usually faster and easier to read than traditional instruments. However, every device must be properly calibrated to ensure accurate results.

Without measuring devices, it would be difficult to build safe structures, conduct scientific experiments, manufacture products, or monitor a person’s health. They help people make informed decisions and maintain consistent standards.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract describing a measuring device that determines the relative position of two bodies using a scale band with uniquely inclined marker-stripe transitions and two detection sensors.
counterfactuals.output: A measuring device for determining a relative position of first and second bodies comprises a scale band coupled to the first body and extending along a measurement direction, and a detector coupled to the second body. The scale band includes a sequence of marker stripes having optically distinguishable regions, transitions between adjacent regions being inclined relative to the measurement direction. At least selected transitions have respective, uniquely defined inclinations and/or inclination sequences encoding corresponding positions along the scale band. The detector includes first and second sensors spaced apart transversely and/or longitudinally with respect to the scale band and configured to detect passage of the transitions during relative movement of the bodies. A processing unit evaluates detection signals from the sensors, including a timing, phase, or position difference associated with a detected transition, to identify its inclination and thereby determine an encoded position. Successive detections may additionally provide displacement magnitude and movement direction. The device thus permits compact, contactless determination of relative position using a robust scale pattern and two detection channels.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in precise technical language with numbered reference signs, an encoder system in which a scale band attached to one body is read by sensors attached to another body.
counterfactuals.output:
### Encoder System

An encoder system **(100)** comprises a first body **(110)** and a second body **(120)** that are movable relative to one another along a measurement direction **(X)**.

A scale band **(130)** is fixed to the first body **(110)** and extends along the measurement direction **(X)**. The scale band **(130)** carries a machine-readable scale pattern **(132)** comprising a succession of scale features **(134)** arranged at predetermined spatial intervals. The scale pattern **(132)** may be optical, magnetic, inductive, capacitive, or otherwise electromagnetically detectable.

At least one sensor assembly **(140)** is fixed to the second body **(120)** and positioned opposite the scale band **(130)** across a reading gap **(G)**. The sensor assembly **(140)** includes one or more sensing elements **(142)** configured to detect the scale features **(134)** as the first and second bodies **(110, 120)** undergo relative displacement. Where multiple sensing elements **(142)** are provided, they may be offset in the measurement direction **(X)** to generate phase-displaced measurement signals.

A signal-processing circuit **(150)** is connected to the sensor assembly **(140)** and configured to derive, from sensor output signals **(S1, S2)**, a position value **(P)** representative of the relative position of the first body **(110)** and the second body **(120)**. The signal-processing circuit **(150)** may determine incremental displacement by counting transitions or interpolating periodic signals associated with the scale pattern **(132)**. An absolute reference feature **(136)** or an absolute code track **(138)** may additionally be provided on the scale band **(130)** to establish an absolute position or reference position.

The scale band **(130)** is retained on a mounting surface **(112)** of the first body **(110)** by an attachment layer **(160)**, mechanical clamps **(162)**, or both. A guide arrangement **(170)** constrains the relative movement of the bodies **(110, 120)** such that the sensor assembly **(140)** remains within a specified operating distance and alignment tolerance relative to the scale band **(130)**.

An output interface **(180)** communicates the position value **(P)** to an external controller **(190)**. The output interface **(180)** may provide digital position data, incremental quadrature signals, analog interpolation signals, or a serial communications signal.

counterfactuals.output:
### Proposed European Patent Wording

#### Title

**Position-measuring device comprising a scale band having angularly encoded marker transitions**

#### Independent apparatus claim

1. **A position-measuring device for determining a relative position between a first body and a second body**, the position-measuring device comprising:  
   
   a scale band arranged on or coupled to the first body and extending in a measuring direction, the scale band comprising a plurality of patterned marker stripes; and  
   
   a sensor arrangement arranged on or coupled to the second body and comprising a first marker-detection sensor and a second marker-detection sensor, the scale band and the sensor arrangement being movable relative to one another in the measuring direction,  
   
   **characterised in that**  
   
   the patterned marker stripes define transitions having respective angular orientations relative to the measuring direction, at least some of the transitions being distinguishable from one another by their angular orientations;  
   
   the patterned marker stripes define a first trace and a second trace extending along the scale band;  
   
   the first marker-detection sensor is arranged to detect the transitions in the first trace and the second marker-detection sensor is arranged to detect the transitions in the second trace; and  
   
   the position-measuring device is configured to determine the relative position of the first and second bodies from detection signals generated by the first and second marker-detection sensors in response to the transitions.

#### Dependent claims

2. The position-measuring device according to claim 1, wherein each of a plurality of the transitions has an angular orientation that is unique within a predetermined region of the scale band.

3. The position-measuring device according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the angular orientations of the transitions encode respective absolute positions along the scale band.

4. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the first trace and the second trace are mutually spaced in a direction transverse to the measuring direction.

5. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the first and second marker-detection sensors are arranged at respective positions corresponding to the first and second traces.

6. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the first and second traces comprise respective portions of common marker stripes extending between the first and second traces.

7. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein a relative displacement between the detection of a transition by the first marker-detection sensor and the detection of the transition by the second marker-detection sensor is indicative of the angular orientation of the transition.

8. The position-measuring device according to claim 7, comprising a processing unit configured to determine the angular orientation of the transition from a difference between respective detection positions or detection times associated with the first and second marker-detection sensors.

9. The position-measuring device according to claim 8, wherein the processing unit is configured to associate the determined angular orientation with a stored position value.

10. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the patterned marker stripes comprise optically detectable regions, and wherein the first and second marker-detection sensors comprise optical sensors.

11. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the two traces provide mutually independent position signals.

12. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the detection signals associated with the first and second traces are combined to determine at least one of an absolute position, a direction of movement, a displacement or a speed of relative movement between the first and second bodies.

13. The position-measuring device according to any preceding claim, wherein the scale band is flexible and is secured to a surface of the first body.

#### Independent method claim

14. **A method of determining a relative position between a first body and a second body**, using a scale band coupled to the first body and a sensor arrangement coupled to the second body, the scale band comprising patterned marker stripes defining first and second traces, and the sensor arrangement comprising first and second marker-detection sensors, the method comprising:

   moving the scale band and the sensor arrangement relative to one another in a measuring direction;

   detecting, by the first marker-detection sensor, transitions of the patterned marker stripes in the first trace;

   detecting, by the second marker-detection sensor, transitions of the patterned marker stripes in the second trace;

   determining respective angular orientations of at least some of the transitions from detection signals generated by the first and second marker-detection sensors, the transitions being distinguishable from one another by their angular orientations; and

   determining the relative position of the first and second bodies on the basis of the determined angular orientations.

15. The method according to claim 14, wherein determining an angular orientation comprises determining a spatial or temporal offset between detection of a transition in the first trace and detection of the transition in the second trace.

16. The method according to claim 14 or 15, comprising assigning the determined angular orientation to an absolute position value.

#### Abstract

A position-measuring device determines a relative position between first and second bodies. A scale band coupled to the first body comprises patterned marker stripes defining first and second traces. A sensor arrangement coupled to the second body comprises first and second marker-detection sensors associated respectively with the first and second traces. Transitions of the patterned marker stripes have angular orientations relative to a measuring direction, at least some of the transitions being distinguishable by their angular orientations. Signals generated by the two sensors upon relative movement of the scale band and the sensor arrangement are evaluated to determine the angular orientations of the transitions and thereby determine the relative position of the bodies.
